official_measurement_examples.name: 1 July 2026 buffer rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: For decision-making from 1 July 2026, a 20% buffer can also apply where a recently adopted requirement examined under a pre-12-December-2024 Framework is 80% or less of the most up-to-date local housing need figure.

official_measurement_examples.name: Latest national HDT publication
official_measurement_examples.fact: As of 26 July 2026, the GOV.UK Housing Delivery Test collection still lists the 2023 measurement as the latest national published measurement; later results must not be fabricated.

official_measurement_examples.name: HDT and 5YHLS separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Housing Delivery Test measures past delivery over a rolling period while five-year supply assesses deliverable forward supply; the two calculations are related but not interchangeable.

official_measurement_examples.name: Threshold consequences
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current guidance links under-95% delivery to an action plan, under-85% to a 20% buffer, and under-75% to the presumption consequence, subject to current policy context.

official_measurement_examples.name: Authority-level context
official_measurement_examples.fact: A five-year housing land supply result is primarily an authority or plan-area planning-policy context and does not itself grant permission to an individual parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Deliverable-site evidence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Inclusion in supply evidence requires deliverability evidence but does not prove current title ownership, exact parcel boundary, infrastructure capacity or final scheme yield.

official_measurement_examples.name: June 2026 examination templates
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate published housing-land-supply evidence templates on 1 June 2026 for different transitional Framework contexts; the relevant policy version must be retained.

official_measurement_examples.name: Recalculation limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: An HDT measurement can be recalculated after adoption of a new housing requirement, so a national table snapshot may not be the current authority-specific consequence without checking local evidence.

core_rules: five-year housing land supply is not parcel planning permission
HDT and five-year supply are distinct calculations
latest national HDT publication must not be inferred beyond published data
1 July 2026 buffer rule must retain effective date and conditions
deliverable-site inclusion is not title ownership proof
deliverable-site inclusion is not exact development yield
authority-level shortfall does not automatically approve every site
presumption consequences still require proposal-specific decision making
HDT thresholds must retain current policy context
local re-runs can supersede a national snapshot for an authority
transitional Framework version must be retained
Planning Data research status is not an authoritative authority result
no parcel housing-supply clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, Planning Inspectorate, GOV.UK and Planning Data sources checked on 2026-07-26. The 1 July 2026 buffer rule, 1 June 2026 evidence templates and latest-published 2023 HDT measurement status were retained with authority/parcel and forward/backward-looking separation; no parcel promotion.
